A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same FedOne paper, including all 33 pages and Appendices A–C. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison; no material gaps were found.

before.justification: v1 reports original MNIST experiments, federated prompt-learning evaluations with RoBERTa-large and GPT-3.5 Turbo, and supplementary query-efficiency, prompt-length, heterogeneity and scalability experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendix C, including performance scores, resource measurements and experimental plots.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Algorithm 1 retain the same Gumbel-Softmax parameterization, variance-reduced policy-gradient updates, aggregation procedure and single-client activation rule. No method component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST and the same seven GLUE tasks: MNLI, QQP, SST-2, MRPC, CoLA, QNLI and RTE. The IID and heterogeneous-client scenarios in Appendix C are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within corresponding experiments. Tables 1–3 and 7 retain the same standalone and federated comparisons, including PromptTuning, P-Tuning v2, BBT, and the GPT-3.5 no-prompt and untrained-prompt controls.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B–C retain the same models, client configurations, k-shot setup, learning-rate grid, batch size, optimizer, metrics and testing procedures. Neither existing protocols nor experimental settings are revised.

E4.justification: The MNIST illustration and Appendix C analyses of activated-client counts, prompt length, client heterogeneity and scalability are retained unchanged. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report three seeds for Tables 1 and 7, 20 repetitions with outlier removal in Appendix C.1, five runs with standard-deviation error bars in C.2, and three repetitions in C.3. Uncertainty reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and plotted findings are retained. For example, FedOne-GS-BDPL averages remain 54.90 in Table 1 and 64.28 in Table 3; Table 6 retains 528.6 ± 382.4 queries for single-client Fed-BDPL.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Assumptions 3.1–3.3, Theorem 3.4, Corollaries 3.5–3.6, and all Appendix A lemmas, derivations and proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims of a first convergence analysis for federated BDPL and optimal query efficiency through activating one client per round. Contribution scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of experimental results, query-cost versus convergence trade-off, bounded-heterogeneity qualification and broader applicability discussion in Section 6 are identical. No substantive limitation or qualification is added.

D1.justification: The implementation link, hyperparameter descriptions, BBT configuration, GPT-3.5 label-token query procedure and appendix experiment details are unchanged. No reproducibility information or resource-access instruction is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 5, the cited works and reference list are unchanged. Both versions position query efficiency and convergence analysis against prior federated prompt-learning research in the same way.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v1 dated 17 June 2025 to v2 dated 23 September 2025. Embedded author metadata corrects Maxwell J. Yin's name and includes Yi Chang, both already present in the visible v1 byline. Prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–6, Tables 1–8 and Algorithm 1 retain their contents, placement, captions and display structure. Axes, legends and page layout are unchanged apart from negligible PDF rendering differences.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the methods, theoretical arguments, empirical evidence and exposition, including all appendices. The version/date update and author-metadata correction do not meaningfully change the paper's rigor, evidential support, reproducibility or readability.
